name: GitHub Repository Analysis - UX Designer
description: Parsing rules for GitHub repositories belonging to UX Designer candidates. UX design work is significantly less code-dense than engineering roles — the primary GitHub signals for UX Designers are design system code contributions, design tooling scripts, exported design artifacts, documentation of behavioral design processes, and UX-adjacent development work (front-end prototypes, data analysis scripts for A/B tests). NOTE: Specific evidence mappings (regex patterns and maps_to composite keys) are stored within individual skill files under evidence.github, NOT here.

target_files.notes: Exported Figma/Sketch files, design token files, or design system exports indicate active tooling proficiency
Customer experience maps or journey map artifacts in any format (PDF, PNG, MD)
BPMN or EPC process model files (camunda .bpmn XML, draw.io exports)
User persona documents, JTBD artifacts, or behavioral research outputs
Wireframe exports, mockup images, or prototype documentation
A/B test documentation, experiment hypotheses, or funnel analysis scripts
Design system contributions indicate systematic, scalable design thinking
Data analysis scripts for behavioral metrics, funnel analysis, or A/B test result processing
Written UX case studies documenting behavioral design process and rationale
Process modeling documentation in any format

behavioral_framework_signals.pattern: Fogg|B=MAP|Hook Model|CREATE Action|Dual Process|System 1|System 2|Nudge Theory|Behavioral Economics|habit loop|Cue-Routine-Reward
behavioral_framework_signals.notes: Named behavioral frameworks in design documentation, READMEs, or case studies
Persuasive pattern terminology in design documentation or code comments

behavioral_framework_signals.pattern: A/B test|split test|p-value|confidence interval|statistical significance|multivariate|HEART framework|North Star
behavioral_framework_signals.notes: Experimentation and metrics terminology in documentation or analysis scripts

behavioral_framework_signals.pattern: Business Model Canvas|Lean Canvas|SWOT|Five Forces|competitor analysis|Porter
behavioral_framework_signals.notes: Strategic framework references in product strategy or design discovery documentation

behavioral_framework_signals.pattern: user story|acceptance criteria|product backlog|Given.*When.*Then|MoSCoW|progressive disclosure|cognitive load|Goal Gradient
behavioral_framework_signals.notes: UX planning and principles terminology in design process documentation
Behavior change strategy terminology in design documentation

repository_types.notes: Design system ownership is a strong signal of systematic, scalable UX practice
Portfolio sites with embedded case studies are high-value UX evidence
Data analysis repositories demonstrate quantitative UX measurement capability
Code-based prototypes demonstrate design implementation depth

tasks: Prioritize qualitative content analysis over file-type scanning — UX GitHub repos are documentation and artifact-heavy rather than code-heavy
Flag repositories with behavioral framework terminology in READMEs or documentation as high-relevance
Distinguish between UX portfolio repos (case studies) and engineering repos a UX designer contributed to — the former is primary UX evidence
When Jupyter notebooks or Python scripts are present, check if they analyze UX/behavioral data (funnel analysis, cohort analysis, A/B test results) vs unrelated data science work
Look for evidence of cross-disciplinary work: UX designers who commit to design system repos or contribute HTML/CSS to prototypes show fuller craft depth
Process modeling files (.bpmn, draw.io exports) are strong UX deliverable evidence — note their presence and complexity
